title: Coordinates
summary: Rill is home, healing, and still reciting numbers in her sleep — but Pem has cross-checked them against terraform-era survey grids. They're an address, and reading it takes three dead survey pylons: the ridge gauge, the drowned cairn, and a marker out past the far glass hills. Hold each one slow and steady, and the old grid will draw you a door.

objectives.label: Hold at the old storm gauge — first pylon reading
Hold at the drowned cairn — second pylon reading
Hold at the old survey point — third pylon, triangulate
Ride the triangulation out to the gate approach

offer.text: Ash! Come in, sit — no, stay standing, I'm told pacing helps the numbers come out. Four-one-seven. Mark. See? That's not me, that's the cave talking through me. Pem says I've been carrying somebody's street directions in my skull for a week.

Station — Pem. The coordinates are old survey grid, terraform-era. Three pylons still hold a whisper of charge: the ridge gauge, the drowned cairn, and a marker past the far glass hills. Read all three and the boxes will draw you a door.
So the cave made Rill a postal worker. Fine. Three pylons, one door. And when we find the door — do we knock?
Nine-one-two, mark — ugh. Sorry. Knock *gently*, Ash. Whatever's behind it has been asleep longer than Saltmouth's been awake.

accept.text: Ketch here. Take the scouting slow — the pylons need a held reading, not a flyby. Hover close, keep the Wren steady, let the box listen. And kid? Write down anything the desert tells you. That's garage policy now.
Rill on the garage couch, medically supervised and *bored*. If the pylons start reciting back, tell them I said nine-one-two. They'll know what it means. I certainly don't.

complete.text: Third reading's in. The grid lines cross past the glass hills — there's a structure out there big enough to fog my visor from this range. It looks… sealed. Patient. Like it's been saving my seat.
The Door, courier. Every survey map we own circles it like a secret. You have done in one afternoon what the Choir has hummed at for two hundred years. Humbling. *So* humbling.
Mark it, seal it, and tell nobody with a treasury. …Kid, I can hear the factions leaning in from here. Now that it's got an address, nothing about that door stays uncounted for long.
